6) Attached terms. Exhibit A forms part of this agreement. Resolve blank information and attach required disclosures and addenda before a live signing request.

7) Agreement and property. Seller agrees to sell and Purchaser agrees to buy the property identified in the Deal Terms and its stated legal description, together with included fixtures, subject to this agreement and signed addenda. All required owners and authorized representatives must sign. No title or authority is presumed from a data-provider record.

8) Cash price and escrow. The purchase price is the agreed price in Deal Terms, payable in available funds through the named closing agent. No financing contingency is created. Do not pay an AI-generated account or wire instruction; verify escrow instructions independently.

9) Inspection and cancellation. Purchaser has the stated inspection period after the effective date to inspect and deliver written termination notice to Seller and escrow. Any required option fee, delivery method, notice deadline or state-specific cancellation language must be supplied before live use. After that period, a change of mind alone does not create a termination right.

10) Title, condition and closing. Sale is as-is, subject to inspection, title contingencies and mandatory disclosures. Seller must convey marketable, insurable title subject only to accepted exceptions. An unresolved material title defect permits Purchaser to terminate before closing, subject to applicable signed terms. Closing is within 30 calendar days after the effective date unless a different date is stated in Deal Terms or agreed by signed amendment. The effective date is the date of the last required signature.

11) Costs, tenants and possession. Buyer pays closing charges legally allocable to Buyer. Seller remains responsible for existing mortgages, liens, unpaid obligations and charges law requires Seller to pay unless separately agreed. Tax and other prorations must appear in the settlement statement. Occupancy, tenant rights, leases, security deposits, access and possession must be addressed in a signed addendum if applicable. No tenant eviction or vacant possession is promised merely because this agreement is signed.

12) Assignment and disclosure. Purchaser acts as a principal, may assign its contractual purchasing interest where permitted, and may earn an assignment fee. Purchaser does not represent Seller and is not offering to sell property it already owns. Required written equitable-interest disclosures and any required assignment consent must be delivered before the relevant transaction. Assignment does not release Purchaser from this agreement without Seller's written consent.

13) Default and withdrawal. A cash buyer's withdrawal does not itself cancel this purchase agreement or extend its deadlines. A party requesting cancellation must identify a contractual or legal basis and deliver required notices; otherwise a written mutual release may be needed. Remedies follow this agreement and applicable law.

14) Access, disclosures and changes. Inspections and buyer showings require Seller/occupant permission; no unannounced visits or destructive testing without consent. Attach required seller disclosures, lead-based-paint disclosures when applicable, state addenda, occupancy terms and agreed special conditions. Mandatory rights prevail. Amendments, deadline extensions and releases must be in a signed writing. Material unresolved issues go to the parties and closing agent for review.
